new_claims.statement: For Q=a(X+m(Y))^2+R(Y), a physical residual cross block with regularized-determinant parameter q and r>q singular values >=sigma implies ||p_Q||_infinity <= [sqrt(e)/(2^(3/4)q^(1/4)) Beta(1/4,(r-q)/(4q))]/sqrt(|a|sigma).
For two residual cross singular values s1,s2 and q<2, square lift pays (s1 s2)^(-1/4), not the smallest singular value alone.
The account02/B01 no-leverage residual density bound plus the square half-Riesz bathtub estimate yields ||p_Q||_infinity <=2 sqrt(2 M_R/|a|).

stress_test.result: For m>=4, bank-halving gives q=1 and a uniform bound <=10.387455 via QFORM-RIESZ-SQUARE-LIFT-v1.

first_unproved_step: Derive from the sole three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis a dimension-free heavy/diffuse decomposition forcing one of the established analytic exits without paying a tiny selected pivot/minor. In the local rank-two square-assisted subproblem, the remaining exceptional boundary is leverage one on both sides together with zero transverse kernel curvature.
next_attempt: Analyze the leverage-one/zero-transverse-curvature boundary structurally and test whether it forces coordinate-supported hyperbolic-square aggregation or an exact block decomposition that can be controlled before reciprocal minor payment.
